pages.title: Weekly Worship
pages.summary: Gather for worship, prayer, Holy Communion and fellowship in the parish churches.

sections.title: A place to worship together
paragraphs: The parish describes its services as opportunities to gather as Christians, worship, encourage one another and share in the life of the wider Church. Sunday worship includes prayer, Holy Communion and fellowship.

The previous parish service guide described a pattern of services at St Michael and All Angels and the Chapel of Ease. As service patterns can change, please use the live calendar or contact the parish to confirm the next service before travelling.

sections.title: Find a service
paragraphs: The Calendar is the current source for dated services and events. The Sunday Services page provides more detail about the pattern recorded on the previous parish website; some arrangements need confirmation.

pages.title: Baptisms
pages.summary: Baptism welcomes children and adults into the Christian faith and the life of the church.

sections.title: A welcome into the church
paragraphs: The parish’s previous information welcomed children and adults to consider baptism, also called christening, as a way of entering the Christian faith. It invited people who live in the parish or have a strong connection with the church to make contact.
The earlier page described baptisms within a Sunday service. Please contact the church to confirm current arrangements, preparation and availability.

sections.title: Start a conversation
paragraphs: If you are thinking about baptism for yourself or a child, the parish can explain the next steps and answer your questions.

pages.title: Weddings
pages.summary: Begin a conversation with the parish if you are considering a church wedding.

sections.title: A church wedding
paragraphs: The parish welcomes enquiries from people thinking about getting married at St Michael and All Angels. The church’s earlier information directed couples to contact the wedding coordinator.
Eligibility, dates, preparation and fees depend on current Church of England guidance and individual circumstances. Contact the parish to discuss your situation and confirm present arrangements.

pages.title: Funerals and remembrance
pages.summary: A place to begin when you are arranging a funeral or seeking prayer and support.

sections.title: With care and compassion
paragraphs: The parish marks significant occasions, including funerals, for members of the church and the wider community. If someone has died, you may speak with your funeral director or contact the parish to ask about a service and the support available.
Arrangements depend on current availability and circumstances. The parish can discuss the options with you.

pages.title: Prayer
pages.summary: Prayer is part of the worship and shared life of the parish.

sections.title: Prayer at St Michael’s
paragraphs: The parish’s worship information describes prayer as part of gathering together, alongside Scripture, Holy Communion and fellowship. The church is a place to pause, reflect and bring what is on your heart.
The previous services page listed a quiet service of Compline or Night Prayer on selected Tuesdays. As that timetable may have changed, check the Calendar for current dates or contact the parish.

sections.title: A prayer request
paragraphs: If you would like to ask for prayer or speak with someone, contact the church. Please share only information you are comfortable communicating by email.

pages.title: Special Services
pages.summary: Seasonal and occasional services are listed in the parish Calendar when details are confirmed.

sections.title: Worship through the year
paragraphs: The parish welcomes the opportunity to mark significant occasions through worship. Details of forthcoming special services should be checked in the Calendar, which is the current source for dates and times.

pages.title: Children & Families
pages.summary: Children and families are warmly welcomed into worship and parish life.

sections.title: Worship together
paragraphs: The parish’s previous service information welcomed families at services and described a carpeted area with resources for children. It also mentioned a creche in the vestry at some services. Please contact the church to confirm what is currently available.
The older service guide described a family service as part of its monthly pattern; check the Calendar for current arrangements.

sections.title: Baptism
paragraphs: The parish welcomes enquiries about baptism for children and adults. Read the Baptisms page to learn more and contact the church about current arrangements.

sections.title: Safeguarding
paragraphs: The church takes safeguarding seriously. If you have a question or concern, use the Safeguarding link in the site footer or contact the parish through the Contact page.

pages.title: Alpha Course
pages.summary: A welcoming space to explore the basics of Christian faith, ask questions and share your point of view.

sections.title: What is Alpha?
paragraphs: The parish describes Alpha as a series of sessions exploring the basics of Christian faith. It is for anyone who would like to explore, ask questions and share their point of view, whatever their background or context.

sections.title: What happens at a session?
paragraphs: The format described by the parish begins with tea and cake, followed by a short film presentation on a question about Christian faith and time for discussion. The course material explores topics including Jesus, prayer, faith, the Holy Spirit, the Bible and how God guides us.

sections.title: Who is Alpha for?
paragraphs: Alpha is intended for people who want space to explore Christian faith and ask questions. You do not need to have everything worked out before you come.

sections.title: Ask about a future course
paragraphs: The old website listed a course contact and dates that may no longer be current, so no course date or named contact is shown here. Please use the Contact page to ask whether a new course is planned.

pages.title: Bible Study & Fellowship
pages.summary: The parish’s fellowship groups make space for Bible study, honest conversation, friendship and spiritual growth.

sections.title: Learning and growing together
paragraphs: The parish describes fellowship and Bible study groups as an important part of church life. Their purpose is to make room for personal discovery and spiritual growth as people learn, ask questions and share the joys and challenges of Christian life.

The previous website described small groups meeting in Westhumble, with weekly gatherings at specific times. Those times and contacts may be out of date, so please ask the parish about current groups before making plans.

sections.title: Everyone is welcome
paragraphs: These groups were described as informal and welcoming, with time for conversation and refreshments. Contact the parish to ask whether a group is currently meeting and whether it would suit you.

pages.title: Pastoral Care
pages.summary: The parish seeks to care for one another through spiritual support, practical help and encouragement.

sections.title: Care within the parish
paragraphs: The parish describes a community where people seek to share one another’s burdens and offer spiritual support, practical help and encouragement. The older team page listed a Parish Visitor role for pastoral care; the named contact may have changed.

If you would like to speak with someone, contact the parish and ask about current pastoral support. The church will respond as it is able; this page does not promise a particular service or response time.

sections.title: Privacy and safeguarding
paragraphs: The parish says it respects privacy and places importance on confidentiality and safeguarding. Please use the Contact page for current information and share only details needed to make your enquiry.

pages.title: Volunteering
pages.summary: Many gifts and practical contributions help support the life of a church community.

sections.title: Taking part
paragraphs: The parish describes church life as a shared effort in which people use their time, talents and resources to serve one another and the wider community. The old site does not provide a current list of volunteer roles.

If you would like to offer help, contact the parish to ask what is currently needed. Any role, training, time commitment and safeguarding requirements should be agreed with the church before it begins.

pages.title: Supporting the Community
pages.summary: The parish seeks to serve people in Mickleham and Westhumble through community life and mutual care.

sections.title: A community of care
paragraphs: The church describes its community life as including practical care, social outreach, courses and pastoral support. The old website does not set out a current directory of support services or partner organisations.
For a current enquiry, contact the parish. The church can let you know what support or signposting is available at present.

pages.title: Our Vision
pages.summary: Inspired by God’s love, the parish seeks to grow spiritually, make Jesus Christ known and welcome people at the heart of the community.

sections.title: Inspired by God’s love
paragraphs: The parish vision is: “Inspired by God’s Love we seek to grow spiritually, make Jesus Christ known and be a loving, inclusive and welcoming church, at the heart of the community.”
This vision connects worship, spiritual growth, welcome and service in Mickleham and Westhumble.

pages.title: Our Churches
pages.summary: The Parish of Mickleham includes St Michael and All Angels in Mickleham and the Chapel of Ease in Westhumble.

sections.title: St Michael and All Angels, Mickleham
paragraphs: The parish describes St Michael and All Angels as a historic church at the heart of Mickleham, with Christian worship on the site for more than a thousand years. The church is listed Grade II* according to the old parish website. See Our History for the historical account.

sections.title: The Chapel of Ease, Westhumble
paragraphs: Westhumble is the parish’s second church. The old website describes the Chapel of Ease as a former barn and notes a much older chapel ruin further up the lane. See the Westhumble Chapel page for the existing account; details should be checked with the parish before a visit.

sections.title: Part of a wider benefice
paragraphs: The old parish welcome describes Mickleham as part of the United Benefice of Leatherhead and Mickleham within the Diocese of Guildford and the Church of England. Please confirm current organisational wording with the parish.

pages.title: Our Team
pages.summary: The parish is served by clergy, churchwardens, staff and volunteers across worship and community life.

sections.title: Clergy and parish leadership
paragraphs: The previous team directory listed a Parish Priest, churchwardens and a deputy churchwarden. These roles serve the worshipping community and help care for the parish churches.

sections.title: Parish administration and PCC
paragraphs: The old directory also listed a Parish Administrator, PCC Secretary and Treasurer, alongside members of the Parochial Church Council. Current office holders and responsibilities should be confirmed by the parish.

sections.title: Worship and music
paragraphs: The earlier team page named an organist and people serving in worship-related roles. Names and arrangements are not repeated here until confirmed.

sections.title: Life events
paragraphs: The old directory listed coordinators for baptism, weddings and funerals. Contact the parish for the current enquiry route for each.

sections.title: Pastoral care and safeguarding
paragraphs: The older team page named a Parish Visitor for pastoral care and a Parish Safeguarding Officer. Current contacts must be confirmed; see the separate Pastoral Care and Safeguarding pages.

sections.title: Electoral Roll and parish magazine
paragraphs: The previous directory also listed an Electoral Roll Officer and parish magazine editors. Contact the parish to confirm the current role-holders and how to get in touch.

sections.title: Get in touch
paragraphs: This page intentionally uses role-based information rather than publishing personal phone numbers or email addresses from an older directory. Use the Contact page for the current parish contact directory.

pages.title: The Electoral Roll
pages.summary: The Electoral Roll is the parish’s formal list of lay members of the Church of England who meet the eligibility requirements.

sections.title: What it is
paragraphs: Each Church of England parish maintains an Electoral Roll. Being on the roll records a person’s connection with the parish and allows them to take part in the parish’s governance, subject to the Church’s rules.

sections.title: Who can apply
paragraphs: Eligibility depends on the Church of England’s current rules, including age, baptism and a qualifying connection with the parish or regular worship. Please ask the Electoral Roll Officer or parish for the current application form and guidance.

sections.title: Applications and privacy
paragraphs: The previous website named an Electoral Roll Officer and included information connected to a past APCM. Dates and contact details may be out of date, so no deadline or named officer is published here. Contact the parish to ask how to apply and how Electoral Roll information is handled.

pages.title: Eco Church
pages.summary: The old parish website linked to Eco Church information; current accreditation and activity details need confirmation.

sections.title: Caring for creation
paragraphs: The previous parish website included an Eco Church section and an award image. The current status, award level and related activities have not been verified for this migration.
The parish can share current information about its environmental work when confirmed. For now, contact the church if you would like to ask about this area of parish life.

pages.title: Safeguarding
pages.summary: The parish’s safeguarding policy sets out its commitment to a safer church for children, young people and adults.

sections.title: A safer church
paragraphs: The safeguarding statement published on the previous parish website says the church is committed to promoting a safer environment, safe recruitment and support, responding promptly to concerns, and offering pastoral care to people affected by abuse or allegations.
It also describes working with the incumbent, the Parochial Church Council, the Diocesan Safeguarding Adviser and statutory agencies when concerns arise.

sections.title: Policy and contacts
paragraphs: The previous policy page said it was agreed in November 2021 and reviewed annually, with the next review stated as July 2026. That review date has passed, so the policy and local contact details need parish confirmation.
Read the existing parish safeguarding statement for the current published policy and contact information. If you have an immediate safeguarding concern, use the appropriate statutory services.

pages.title: Privacy & GDPR
pages.summary: The parish publishes privacy information separately from general visitor information.

sections.title: Privacy information
paragraphs: The previous parish website provides a separate Privacy Statement. Its text was not available for this migration review, so it has not been rewritten or summarised here.
Use the parish’s existing privacy statement for its published information while the current notice is confirmed for this website.

pages.title: The Church Building
pages.summary: Explore the historic fabric of St Michael and All Angels through the parish’s account of the building.

sections.title: Historic fabric
paragraphs: The parish history describes a church with early Saxon traces and substantial Norman and medieval fabric. Among the features it records are the chancel arch, chancel lancet windows, stone font, Norbury Chapel, medieval tombstones, carved pulpit and six bells.

The building has been altered over the centuries. Read the fuller Our History account for the parish’s notes on restorations and historic features. Please confirm current opening and visitor arrangements before making a special journey.

pages.title: The Churchyard
pages.summary: The churchyard is a place of remembrance and a part of Mickleham’s local history.

sections.title: A place of remembrance
paragraphs: The old parish website describes the churchyard as a place of beauty and historical value and points to a guide to its oldest part. It also publishes detailed churchyard regulations covering burials, memorials, flowers and the Book of Remembrance.

Those regulations were stated as approved by the PCC on 7 November 2023. Because local rules and availability can change, contact the parish for the current regulations, forms and advice before arranging a memorial, planting or burial.

pages.title: Churchyard Regulations
pages.summary: Ask the parish for the current approved churchyard regulations and forms before making arrangements.

sections.title: Current rules and advice
paragraphs: The previous parish website published regulations approved by the Mickleham Parochial Church Council on 7 November 2023. They cover burial eligibility, memorials, flowers, planting, cremated remains and the Book of Remembrance.
As these rules are locally approved and date-sensitive, this page does not reproduce them as current. Please contact the parish for the latest version and any required forms before taking action.

pages.title: Norman Architecture
pages.summary: The parish history identifies several Norman features within St Michael and All Angels.

sections.title: Features described in the parish history
paragraphs: The parish history describes the chancel arch as Norman, with chevron and dog-tooth ornament, and records the chancel lancet windows and stone font as early features. It places much of the present church in the Norman period, around the late twelfth century.

The same historical account describes earlier Saxon traces and later restoration. For context and the full story, see Our History. This page follows the parish account and is not a formal architectural assessment.

pages.title: Find Us
pages.summary: St Michael and All Angels is on Old London Road in Mickleham; Westhumble Chapel is on Crabtree Lane.

sections.title: St Michael and All Angels, Mickleham
paragraphs: Old London Road, Mickleham, Dorking, Surrey RH5 6DU, England.

The old parish visitor information describes a bike rack by the main entrance and the 465 bus stopping outside the church. It also says Box Hill & Westhumble station is about 1.4 miles away, a walk of around 30 minutes. Bus routes, facilities and journey times can change; check current travel information before setting out.

sections.title: Chapel of Ease, Westhumble
paragraphs: Crabtree Lane, Westhumble, Surrey RH5 6BG. The previous parish website gives this address. Please contact the parish if you need help confirming the precise entrance or current access arrangements.

sections.title: Map and access
paragraphs: Use the map link for directions to St Michael and All Angels. The website does not yet have verified information about step-free access, parking or facilities, so please contact the parish if you need access information before your visit.

pages.title: What to Expect
pages.summary: You are welcome to visit, take your time and join in with worship as much or as little as feels comfortable.

sections.title: A warm welcome
paragraphs: The parish welcomes visitors to its services and activities. You may take time to settle in, sit quietly, and ask someone if you need help.
Service formats vary. Check the Calendar for current service details, and contact the parish if you have a question about what to expect or need to confirm practical arrangements.

pages.title: Mickleham War Memorial
pages.summary: The war memorial stands in the churchyard at St Michael’s and commemorates local people who died in the two world wars.

sections.title: Remembering local history
paragraphs: The old parish website says the Mickleham War Memorial is in the churchyard of St Michael’s and bears the names of 11 men who died in the First World War and 11 who died in the Second World War. The Mickleham & Westhumble Local History Group produced an illustrated booklet with information about those commemorated.
The booklet and memorial details are linked from the earlier parish website. Contact the parish or local history group to confirm current access to the booklet.

pages.title: Parish Magazine
pages.summary: The parish magazine shares news and reflections from across Mickleham and Westhumble.

sections.title: News from across the parish
paragraphs: The old website linked to a current parish magazine edition and identified the magazine as a place for parish and village news. That issue link and editor contacts may now be out of date.

The new website’s News & Magazine section is ready to hold approved articles and updates. Use the News page for current published items; contact the parish if you are looking for a recent magazine edition.
